blind_spots.blind_spot: Selling counter-UAS mitigation capabilities that almost no customer is legally allowed to use
blind_spots.operator_reality: Detection is unregulated; mitigation is not. In the United States, non-kinetic drone defeat — jamming, spoofing, protocol takeover — is limited to a short list of federal authorities (DoD under 10 USC 130i, plus DOE, DHS and DOJ), and every other buyer, including a domestic airport, a stadium or a utility, is barred by the Communications Act. Even inside DoD, transmitting on those bands requires a spectrum supportability determination (DD Form 1494) and a host-nation or installation frequency assignment. A vendor without that package can only ever demo inside a shielded enclosure, which is exactly the shape of a prototype that never fields: the capability works, and the paperwork that would let anyone press the button does not exist.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Takeover and spoofing are the most impressive things to put on a capability slide, and in a demo environment nobody asks who is authorized to radiate — so the constraint only surfaces when a real site visit gets scheduled and then cancelled.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Core Capabilities: Multi-Spectrum SIGINT / Active Drone Takeover / Predictive Analytics / GPS Spoofing / Cyber Infiltration and Deception / Swarm Detection and Defense

blind_spots.blind_spot: A proprietary common operational picture competing with the one the unit already uses
blind_spots.operator_reality: Their architecture terminates in their own C2 layer — 'one coherent operational picture'. The unit already has a picture: TAK on the tablet, FAAD C2 or a service equivalent for air defense, and a watch floor that will not add a second screen with a separate login. In practice the winning move is to stop being a display and become a feed — publish Cursor-on-Target into TAK, push tracks into the existing air picture, and let the operator keep the tool they were trained on. That is a small engineering decision made early and a re-architecture made late, and which one it is decides whether the Phase III has a user.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The commercial and foreign-government maritime customers they also serve have no incumbent COP, so building the whole stack has always been the right answer for the buyer in front of them.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Every layer contributes to one unified operational picture, from orbit to command.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Fusing 500+ satellites' worth of third-party data without visible data-rights or accreditation boundaries
blind_spots.operator_reality: Their value proposition is aggregation — commercial EO, SAR, RF, hyperspectral, VIIRS/MODIS, AIS — through a 'satellite operator data partner network'. Each of those feeds arrives with a license that governs derivative products and onward distribution, and some operators are foreign. A government customer that wants to act on a track has to know it can retain and share the derived product, and a classified customer needs the whole pipeline to run inside an accredited boundary rather than in the vendor's cloud. Neither question is a technology question, and both of them are answered during contracting, not during the demo — which is where the schedule goes.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: In the commercial and ESG-facing side of the business — shipping, insurers, sanctions compliance — imagery licensing is routine and the customer never asks where the pipeline physically runs.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Through our satellite operator data partner network, we can tailor historical surveys and monitoring campaigns towards virtually any threat type.

opener_hook: The Morpheus page lists Active Drone Takeover and GPS Spoofing as core capabilities, and in the US only four federal authorities can lawfully employ either one — which usually means the DD-1494 spectrum package, not the software, is what sets the demo date.
what_they_do: Miami intelligence-fusion company (Space-Eyes) selling three platforms — counter-UAS RF detection, maritime dark-vessel tracking, and wildfire prediction — built on fused commercial satellite, drone and AIS data.
